newsitem.title: UK: Tourism to Britain rises to all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Tourism to Britain rises to all-time high.

text.p: A record three million tourists visited Britain in August, lured by Britain's image as the style capital of Europe, the government said on Wednesday.
"London is universally recognised as a centre of style and innovation. Our fashion, music and culture are the envy of European neighbours," the Department of National Heritage said.
"This abundance of talent, together with our rich heritage, makes "Cool Britannia" an obvious choice for visitors from all over the world."

August is the busiest tourist month of the year. Numbers rose six percent during the month to reach three million for the first time. Tourist numbers in the first eight months of 1996 were 12 percent up on the 1995 period to 17.9 million.
Spending was up by seven per cent to 8.5 billion pounds ($14 billion).

The U.S. weekly news magazine Newsweek last month had a cover story on London's attractions in terms of culture and style, mirroring a belief in the British capital that it has taken over from Paris and Rome as the "must-see" city of European tourist sites. ($1=.6072 Pound)
